summary: Registers an ENUM service for H.323, a framework for multimedia communication over packet networks, following the rules in RFC 3761. This lets a phone number point to an H.323 address. It was updated by RFC 6118.

plainLanguage.summary: This adds one more option to the phone-number lookup list: an address for a certain kind of video or voice call system.

questions: how does enum work with h.323
subtitle: Registers the E2U+H323 ENUM service so a telephone number can map to an H.323 address.

tldr.problem: H.323 multimedia calls over the Internet could use DNS and ENUM to help complete calls, but no ENUM service existed for H.323.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers the service E2U+H323 with the URI scheme h323:, and says the ENUM record MUST hold a standard H.323 URL.
tldr.outcome: A telephone number can now resolve to an H.323 URL. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists RFC 6118 as updating it.

today: RFC 3762 is a Proposed Standard, and RFC 6118 is listed as updating it.

sections.title: Why H.323 Needs ENUM
sections.content:
The H.323 specification defines a means for building multimedia communication services over an arbitrary packet based network, including the Internet. When H.323 is used on the Internet, the author notes it would be useful to use DNS and ENUM to help complete multimedia calls.

This document registers an enumservice for H.323 under the rules in RFC 3761.
sections.plainLanguage: You know a phone number but need the address for an H.323 call. This registers a way to look it up.

sections.title: The Registration Template
sections.content:
Following the template in RFC 3761, the service name is E2U+H323 and the URI scheme is h323:. Intended usage is COMMON, the author is Orit Levin, and there is no other information.

The registration is the only IANA action: the document registers the service according to RFC 3761 and its own definitions.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a form filled in once: the name of the service, what its addresses look like and who wrote it.

sections.title: How the Service Behaves
sections.content:
The H.323 related ENUM record MUST be populated with a standard H.323 URL as defined in H.323. The URL MAY include parameters naming the specific protocols and transport means the H.323 entity supports.

The H.323 entity MUST fully follow the RFC 3761 procedures for record retrieval and processing by the DNS client. If the lookup returns an H.323 URL that matches local policies and capabilities, the procedure in section O.8.1 "Locating H.323 Destination" of H.323 Annex O SHOULD be performed.
sections.plainLanguage: The entry must hold a proper H.323 address. If it fits what your system can do, you go on and place the call.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
Once the h323-URL information is in the DNS, it is effectively publicly accessible. Access to the H.323 destinations can be secured with the techniques in H.235, the security framework for H.323, which covers integrity, authentication, non-repudiation and encryption for H.323 calls.

An analysis of threats specific to ENUM's dependence on DNS, and the applicability of DNSSEC, is provided in RFC 3761.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone can read the directory, so the call itself has to be protected separately.
